thread:
sam_support: FYI escalation from AcmePay — customer sees JSON mode streaming parse failures only on long chat responses. Non-streaming works fine.

sam_support: Error shows 'Unexpected control character (0x00) at line 1 column 128' in Python client. They pasted raw chunks with embedded \u0000 bytes.

olivia_cs: Customer says it started after today's deploy ~09:12 UTC. They sent minimal repro.

maria_sdk: Can you paste the raw stream? need chunk boundaries + content-type headers.

sam_support: Here's the raw sequence they sent (redacted ids):
```
--chunk
{"delta":"Hello, here is a chunk"}
--chunk
{"delta":"more", "n":0}\u0000
--chunk
{"delta":"final"}
```
They claim the Python json-mode parser chokes on the \u0000 after the second JSON object.

sam_support: Attached their Python snippet:
```py
for part in client.responses.stream_json(...):
    text += part['delta']
```

maria_sdk: Hmm. Our Python streaming parser uses a small-state incremental decoder that expects valid UTF-8 and JSON tokens. A literal NUL (0x00) in the middle of the stream will break the C JSON decoder path we use. TS/Go parsers have different behavior.

devon_eng: Do we insert any NULs at the edge? infra would insert separators but not NULs. Lee?

lee_infra: Not intentionally. We do use framing markers when converting internal fast-path chunks to NDJSON for clients; those markers are usually ASCII. No known change today that would insert \u0000.

devon_eng: Can we reproduce locally? sam, can you forward a full dump (including raw bytes, not just escaped string)?

sam_support: Sent the full bytes to the thread DM. Key detail: customer uses a custom reverse-proxy that rewrites some headers and does a small body rewrite (for analytics). Possible their proxy is introducing bytes.

olivia_cs: Customer insists it worked yesterday w/o errors. Their proxy vendor says they didn't deploy anything.

maria_sdk: I ran a quick repro by injecting a 0x00 between JSON objects into our Python stream parser. It indeed raises "Unexpected control character" from the C JSON layer. TS stream parser is tolerant and just emits the objects; Go likewise skips nul bytes in our streaming scanner.

maria_sdk: Two mitigation options:
- Short-term: Make Python streaming parser tolerant by skipping 0x00 separators when not inside a string. Patch is small (pre-scan chunk and strip lone NULs).
- Long-term: Harden the server framing so we never splice raw NULs into streams and add a unit test.

devon_eng: Also check billing/latency impact. If parser hangs, customer may retry and duplicate tokens. Are any errors triggering retries?

sam_support: Customer saw ~2-3 retries which inflated token usage. They're asking for credit for the extra billing and an ETA for fix.

lee_infra: We should confirm whether the NULs are server-side or proxy-introduced before rolling any server change. Patch to client is safe and small; can put out a 0.15.3 hotfix for Python to avoid immediate customer pain.

maria_sdk: I have a draft PR: strip_nuls_in_streaming_decoder. Unit tests included. Will push after review.

devon_eng: If we release client hotfix, we also need to coordinate with docs and changelog and notify support. Also add a short note to streaming best-practices: avoid reverse-proxy body rewrites.

sam_support: I told customer we're looking into it and offered an interim workaround: switch to non-streaming `json` mode call (slower but stable) or upgrade to patched SDK when available. They accepted.

lee_infra: Meanwhile I'll pull request additional logging in the streaming ingress path to capture raw bytes (safe mode: only for this customer id, TTL 24h). If we see zero bytes from upstream we can prove proxy is culpable.

maria_sdk: Quick note about implementation: patch will do a fast memchr for 0x00 then if found, run a linear filter that preserves UTF-8 sequences and removes NUL if it is outside of JSON strings. This avoids altering legitimate \u0000 escapes ("\\u0000") inside strings. Tests cover those cases.

sam_support: Good call on not changing escaped \u0000. Customer reported the bytes as literal NUL, not escape.

olivia_cs: Customer wants credits: they reported +$120 in unexpected tokens from 3 retries. Can finance handle one-off credit pending root cause?

devon_eng: Approve one-off credit for now; if root cause is our server we escalate for full credit.

sam_support: Filed internal ticket RED-4821 for the investigation + customer credit.

maria_sdk: Pushed PR to branch, request review from devon and lee. Change is backwards-compatible and adds ~120 lines. CI green locally.

devon_eng: Quick code comment: avoid copying large buffers on every chunk — use a small scratch buffer and only allocate when we detect a NUL. We don't want perf regressions for normal streams.

maria_sdk: Yep implemented lazy-copy path. Benchmarks show <0.5% overhead on clean streams.

support-bot: Deploy pipeline started for python-sdk 0.15.3-hotfix -> staging. CI: 1/6 failed flakily, rerunning.

maria_sdk: Will monitor staging and post results. If green, push release to pypi and post release note.

lee_infra: Logging PR opened for ingress (short TTL). If logs show no NULs server-side, we'll direct customer to their proxy vendor.

sam_support: Customer asked for ETA. I gave rough timeline: staging verification today, release to pypi tomorrow morning PST, SDK upgrade + retries mitigation.

olivia_cs: Keep me posted — I'll prepare the credit and the customer message once we confirm root cause.

maria_sdk: Staging overall tests passed after rerun. Going to schedule release at 09:00 PST tomorrow.

sam_support: Thanks everyone — holding thread open until post-release confirmation and final root cause.
